RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the December 7, 2007/Agrahayana 16, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
103
Breast feeding promotion measures
*321. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
breast feeding is crucial for the health and
development of the infants and this holds
immense benefits for the mothers as well;
(b) whether lack of awareness on breast
feeding among the common people has been
the major bottleneck in promoting this
practice among the general public; and
(c) if so, what is the action plan of
Government to create awareness among the
general public about the immense benefits
of breast feeding?
Health sector expansion and health
care to old people
*322. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
according to FICCI, India would require an
investment of 78 billion dollars in the next
decade to fund the addition of
approximately 10,00,000 beds which are
needed;
(b) if so, with meagre funding of 1 per
cent of GDP on total healthcare system,
how Government would achieve this target;
(c) what healthcare system his Ministry
is going to evolve for the ageing people and
senior citizens having chronic diseases; and
(d) in what manner, Government is going
to ensure that old age people get cheaper
and accessible medical treatment?
Renewal of Tatkal Scheme
*323. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of RAILW AYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has renewed
the guidelines for the Tatkal Scheme for
reservations;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that reservations
under this scheme can now be obtained two
months in advance against the payment of
a premium;

104
(d) if so, the rationale for such provisions
in the scheme; and
(e) what steps are being taken to ensure
that the seats are made available to
passengers travelling in emergency?
Change in the route of trains
†*324. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Government of
Jharkhand has expressed its displeasure by
objecting to the change in the route of
different trains or their cancellation by
Railways without taking the State
Government into confidence, in the name
of 'Bandh' of Maoists in the State;
(b) the basis of decision of cancelling of
trains or changing their routes; and
(c) at which level is the decision taken
in this regard?
Forceful occupation of seats in trains
by political workers
†*325. SHRI SHATRUGHAN
SINHA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the workers
of various political parties freely travel in
the trains without tickets to take part in
the rallies being organized by the concerned
parties;
(b) whether it is also a fact that these
workers forcibly occupy the seats and
berths of the passengers travelling on valid
tickets and the Railway administration does
not provide any help to the passengers;
and
(c) if so, the action being taken in this
regard?
Failure of MCI to fill up
vacant posts
*326. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether after learning that the
Medical Council of India (MCI) has failed
to implement the directions to fill up the
vacant posts, the Delhi High Court has
directed Health Secretaries of eight States
and Vice-Chancellors of ten universities to
explain the reason for delay in implementing
the orders;
(b) if so, what were the reasons put
forward by the States for not complying
with the orders of the High Court to fill all
the vacancies in the Medical Council;
and
(c) what are the steps now being
considered to implement the orders of the
High Court to fill up all the vacancies?
Declining growth rate of
Agriculture
*327. SHRI RA VULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: W ill the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the growth rate of
agriculture is declining;
(b) if so, the comparative details thereof
during the last three years alongwith the
reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken to improve the
situation of agriculture in future?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

105
Special programme to check the
declining sex ratio
*328. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) is there a steep decline in sex ratio in
India;
(b) if so, what are the special
programmes taken up by his Ministry to
change this trend;
(c) what are the main reasons for this
crisis; and
(d) what is the role assigned to NGOs
to set things right?

RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December 7, 2007/Agrahayana 16, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food and
Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 155
Lesser crop-price by Government than
corporations
†1940. SHRI AJAY SINGH
CHAUTALA: W ill the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that crop-price
given by Government to the farmers is
much less than the prices given by the
corporations to them;
(b) whether Government would advise
the corporations not to purchase crops from
the farmers until and unless Government's
procurement targets are achieved; and
(c) whether Government would issue
the guidelines to ban the import of wheat
and to declare a rational procurement prices
of wheat and other crops?
Cost of agriculture input
1941. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state that
in view of the crash in prices of agricultural
output and the rise in cost of agricultural
input which have adversely affected the
interests of all sections among the
peasantry, what concrete steps Government
propose to take in this regard?
MSP for wheat and pulses
1942. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
substantially increase the Minimum
Support Price (MSP) of wheat and pulses;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the time by which a final decision is
likely to be taken in this regard?
Use of chemical fertilizers
†1943. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the use of
chemical fertilizers such as ammonium
nitrate, potassium sulphate and super
phosphate has increased over 150-fold over
past 50 years;
(b) whether over use of these fertilizers
has led to fall in per-hectare agriculture
production;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

459
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
and efforts being made by Government to
overcome it; and
(d) the measures being taken to promote
bio-fertilizers in place of chemical
fertilizers alongwith the details thereof?
Huge loss of cereal production due to
climate change
1944. SHRIMA TI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
huge loss of cereal production due to
climate change;
(b) if so, whether the ICAR has taken
up any study to assess the loss of cereal
production due to climate change;
(c) if so, the percentage of decline in
the last three years and in the coming
decade;
(d) the details of cereals that are going
to be worst affected due to climate change;
and
(e) what plans his Ministry has to
overcome this situation?
Need to import rice
1945. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that production
of rice would not be able to meet domestic
needs and that the country may have to
resort to import of rice;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether the production of wheat is
sufficient to meet requirement of  those rice
eaters switching to wheat;
(d) if not, the steps being taken to ensure
self-sufficiency in rice and wheat; and
(e) whether the shortfall in rice
production would result in rice eaters
switching to wheat?
Decline in agriculture production
1946. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has received
any report from the State Governments
about decline in agricultural production
and productivity, attributable to division of
agriculture labour from fields to National
Rural Employment Guarantee (NREG)
Scheme;
(b) if so, from which States; and
(c) what is the Government's reaction
and response thereto?
Fodder Bank
1947. SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO
JOSHI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is providing Central funds to the States for
the establishment of fodder banks in the
States to meet the exigencies in natural
calamities;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the funds released to Maharashtra,
so far, for the purpose and the results
achieved therefrom?
Financial assistance for horticulture to
Goa
1948. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any
scheme/schemes to give financial
assistance to the State Governments for the
development of horticulture;

460
(b) if so, the names of the schemes
available with respect to various
plantations/crops;
(c) the essential features of each of the
schemes; and
(d) the details of the financial assistance
given to the Government to Goa in the
matter of each of the schemes, in the last
three years?
Latest farming knowledge to farmers
1949. SHRI A. VIJAY ARAGHAV A
